look_here_first: Cream-white ELONGATED flower SPIKES (rather than round heads of S. roemeriana), distinctive hooked prickles on woody twigs and notably broader/longer leaflets than most Gregg's catclaw. For Gregg versus Wright, measure several mature leaflets and check whether the inflorescence is comparatively loose and whether ripe pods curl.

morphology_keys.habit: Thorny shrub or small tree, locally sometimes tree-sized.
morphology_keys.armature: Short hooked recurved internodal prickles on stems, not paired stipular spines.
morphology_keys.leaves: Bipinnate, often 1–4 pinna pairs and 3–6 leaflet pairs per pinna. Leaflets obovate. The 2024 regional key gives about 5–9(-12) mm long, but its own species description gives 3–6 × 2–3 mm; numeric overlap/inconsistency warrants measuring several fully mature leaves, not a single strict cutoff.
morphology_keys.flowers: Cream to yellowish-white flower SPIKES, elongated rather than spherical, often more open/less compact than Gregg's.
morphology_keys.pods: Broad, flat pods, often slightly constricted; can be distorted or coiled, so curvature alone not definitive.
best_field_traits: Larger round-obovate leaflets than typical Gregg's catclaw
morphology_keys.petiole_gland: A capitate gland is reported at/near the proximal pinna pair; requires a verified tight macro before adding a training arrow.
morphology_keys.pod_confirmation: Usually straight-to-slightly curved in regional key, but detailed 2024 treatment also permits coiled pods. Do not exclude Wright based only on a curled pod.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Roemer forms spherical cream heads. Gregg and Wright have elongated cream flower spikes; Wright often has relatively larger leaflets and a laxer spike, while Gregg more often has tighter spikes and curling pods. The 2024 paper's Wright numeric key (5–9(-12) mm) conflicts partly with its descriptive text (3–6 mm), so teach the RELATIVE traits and request multiple leaves, petiole measures and mature pods before a confident hard-pair determination.
